findings.F1: The failing measure is Calmar (0.62 against 0.75), and it is set by one fall: the book's deepest fall, −2.6 % over 117 days, starts in w14 and ends in w15, and w14 holds the book's two worst days (−2.02 % and −1.50 %, against no other day below −0.56 %); the 15 worst short cases are almost all in w14, with coin rises of 10 to 12 % the next day.
findings.F2: The effect lives in up days that follow a deep 3-day fall: by the 3-day return measured in 30-day swings, the two most negative quartiles of the cases earn +2.0 % and +2.1 % short-side excess next day (48 and 47 cases), while the two shallowest earn −0.8 % and −0.2 % (47 and 48 cases); of the 94 cases with the 3-day return below −0.65 swings, both depth halves earn (+1.8 %, +2.2 %), while the 96 shallower cases lose in both halves (−0.6 %, −0.3 %).
findings.F3: The deep 3-day fall is not an effect of its own: in the profile, on days with the same deep 3-day return but no up day, a short earns −2.7 % (t −4.7, 140 days) and −0.5 % (107 days), against +2.1 % (t 2.6, 49 cases) and +1.8 % (48 cases) when the day rose; only the bounce inside the deep fall gives back.
findings.F4: The falls of w14–w15 come from the shallow cases: the 21 losing cases there had a mean 3-day return of −0.57 swings, a range of 1.13 swings and a depth of 0.45, against −1.15, 1.84 and 0.71 for the 38 winning cases; a rebuilt book keeping only the deep-3-day cases cuts the deepest fall from −2.6 % to −0.91 % and lifts Calmar from 1.05 to 2.42 (Sharpe 1.00 to 1.11, yearly return 2.7 % to 2.2 %, folds B and C, the same rebuild).
findings.F5: The day's range against the 30-day swing is graded too: by quartile of the high-low range, short excess runs −0.86 %, −0.41 %, +1.6 %, +2.6 % (47–48 cases each); the wide range alone is not the effect (in the profile, wide-range days without the signal earn −0.47 % over 471 days, low-range signal days −0.64 % over 98, wide-range signal days +2.1 % over 97), and a rebuilt book with deep 3-day return and wide range together has its deepest fall at −0.91 % and Calmar 2.65.
findings.F6: The close's depth below the high carries the effect only in its top quartile (+2.5 % short excess, 48 cases, against +0.5 %, +0.05 %, −0.1 % in the three lower quartiles), so the tested grading sizes the shallow, losing cases almost as large as the good ones.
findings.F7: The same up-day-in-a-falling-3-days situation outside the falling agitated profile still gives back, though less: +0.46 % short excess, t 2.8, 869 cases, against +1.0 % inside, so the profile concentrates the effect rather than creating it.

ideas.idea: In a falling, agitated market, a coin's up day that comes after a 3-day fall is followed by a fall over the next day, and the deeper that 3-day fall against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days, the larger the next-day fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader shorts the one-day bounce inside an agitated decline only for a day and sizes it by how deep the 3-day fall was, which keeps the book out of the shallow-dip bounces that made its deepest fall.
ideas.name: bounce after deep 3-day fall

ideas.idea: In a falling, agitated market, a coin's up day that comes while its 3-day return is still negative is followed by a fall over the next day, and the wider that day's high-to-low range against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days, the larger the next-day fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader fades the wide, violent bounces in an agitated decline for one day and leaves the narrow ones alone, since a narrow bounce inside a falling 3-day move does not give back.
ideas.name: wide-range bounce fade in decline

ideas.idea: In a falling, agitated market, a coin's up day that comes after a 3-day fall is followed by a fall over the next day, and the larger that day's high-to-low range plus the depth of its 3-day fall, both against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days, the larger the next-day fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader shorts for one day only the bounces that are both wide and come out of a deep 3-day fall, so the position is largest where the give-back is surest and the drawdown smallest.
ideas.name: wide bounce after deep fall
